jobs.title: SLASH · The clipping
jobs.prompt: a single full-page comic drawing (1 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: Behind the frame shop's counter, in the drawer with the pins, a clipping the owner cut from a wire story years ago: a riverboat lost when the ground opened under a Louisiana town. The framer reads it twice and puts it back under the pins. Panel 1: black and white noir comic page, brush-pen over blue pencil, rain as dense vertical hatching, stark black spotting, an open drawer with scattered pushpins and a yellowed newspaper clipping showing a riverboat listing beside a ragged hole in a street, the headline as black blocks, a man's shadow falling across it from a doorway. Owner says "Arthur? You still back there?". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @supporting is the model sheet for THE EDITOR: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_frame_shop shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @supporting for the character the editor; @loc_frame_shop for the setting; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
